arithmetic_intensity_basis: 4 FLOPs per point / 16 DRAM bytes (one 8-byte read + one 8-byte write, ideal reuse). This is the upper bound; with write-allocate it is 0.167 and for the 4-pass NumPy implementation about 0.042, see arithmetic_intensity_flop_per_byte.
kernel: 5-point Jacobi stencil, out = 0.25 * (N + S + W + E)
bandwidth_method: single-process numpy copy of 256 MB, 24 B/element
peak_basis: 8 cores x 2496 MHz x 16 DP FLOP/cycle (AVX2 FMA)
conclusion: AI of 0.250 FLOP/byte (at best) sits far left of the ridge point 7.17 FLOP/byte, and the 32 MB working set exceeds the 13 MB L3, so every sweep streams from DRAM. The kernel is limited by memory bandwidth, not arithmetic: adding cores helps only until the shared memory channels saturate, which is what caps the strong-scaling speedup.
